briefs.text: Oscar Piastri and his long-time managers Mark and Ann Webber have ended their partnership by mutual agreement, saying it was an appropriate time to close it.
Verstappen, Norris, Sainz and Hadjar criticised Pirelli's wet and intermediate tyres after Brazil, and Norris warned the cold in Las Vegas could make things worse.
F1 says it still plans to finish the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi despite Gulf security worries, with Imola reported as a single-race fallback for 6 December.
Google unveiled two more eighth-generation TPU chips, the 8tx for confidential inference and the dual-chip 8i Max, making four new TPU systems this year.

body: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the United States are due to sit down in Abu Dhabi today and tomorrow, the first trilateral meeting since a round in Geneva in February. The process had stalled while Washington was absorbed by the US-Israeli war with Iran. The US side is led by special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Russia has sent presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky with deputy foreign ministers and military intelligence chiefs; Ukraine's team is led by Rustem Umerov, head of its foreign intelligence service, and includes Kyrylo Budanov, now the president's chief of staff.

Europe is not at the main table. National security advisers from Britain, France and Germany, plus EU and NATO officials, will hold separate meetings with the Ukrainian delegation; AFP adds Italy to that list. The Kremlin insists the format is strictly three-way. Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, says security arrangements come first, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that nothing had been finalised.

The core dispute is unchanged. Moscow wants Ukraine to withdraw from the parts of the Donetsk region it still holds, which Kyiv has ruled out, and Volodymyr Zelensky has warned against a deal carved up over Ukraine's head, a 'Yalta 2.0'. Donald Trump has spoken of a very big agreement involving all of Europe and suggested Ukraine may end up a different shape. Fighting continues: Kyiv said 55 people were killed in a frontline village while queuing for aid, and weekend Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands.
Expectations are low on both sides. Watch for whether any limited steps emerge, such as an energy truce or Black Sea arrangements, rather than a full settlement.
stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine and the US meet in Abu Dhabi for first three-way peace talks since February
stories.standfirst: Two days of US-mediated talks open today, with European officials, including Britain's national security adviser, holding separate sessions alongside.

body: Nvidia's board said on Sunday that a committee of independent directors, with outside counsel, will investigate reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. In a memo to staff the same day Huang wrote that he had been unfaithful to his wife and said he supports the inquiry. The woman involved, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data-centre company that advertises a partnership with Nvidia. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she worked for China's Ministry of State Security. China's foreign ministry called the spy claim baseless.

The board says it has no reason to think national security or company secrets were compromised and that it still has confidence in Huang. Donald Trump has defended him. Three Republican congressmen have asked him for a closed-door briefing, and analysts have noted Nvidia has no public succession plan.
The shares fell around 5 per cent on Monday; CBS put the early loss of market value at about $247bn, on top of a roughly 20 per cent slide over the past month.
stories.headline: Nvidia board investigates Jensen Huang after he admits affair with woman US officials call a Chinese spy

sources.name: Nvidia, A Message to Our Company

stories.standfirst: The world's most valuable chipmaker opened an independent probe into its founder and chief executive, and its shares fell about 5 per cent on Monday.

body: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Monday. They are the same underlying model: Fable is the general release, available to all users and through AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, while Mythos has looser cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is limited to vetted organisations. Fable now costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output, down from $10 and $50, and responds up to about 30 per cent faster. Anthropic says over 90 per cent of code merged into its core codebase is now written by Claude under human guidance, and that a team of 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formally verified Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours.

Safety disclosures got as much attention as the features. The system card says Mythos 5.2 seemed aware it might be under test in up to 43 per cent of automated audit transcripts. TechCrunch tied the launch to a METR report suggesting Anthropic's internal models have roughly doubled the pace of its AI progress, a step towards what researchers call recursive self-improvement. The UK AI Security Institute was among the pre-release testers.
stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, cutting Fable's price by a fifth
stories.standfirst: The new top-end models arrive alongside an outside report suggesting AI is now noticeably speeding up Anthropic's own research.

body: The zero emission vehicle mandate requires 80 per cent of new cars sold in 2030 to be fully electric, rising to 100 per cent in 2035. The Guardian reported on Sunday, citing government sources, that the 2030 figure will be cut to around 60 per cent, and Reuters says the mandate's flexibilities could be extended to 2034. Louise Haigh, the prime minister's de facto deputy, is expected to finalise the plan after a meeting on Wednesday. Andy Burnham has stepped back from the decision because his wife advises an EV charging company.
Burnham said on Monday the reports were speculation and no decision had been made. The government says the 2030 end of new petrol and diesel-only car sales and the 2035 goal are not changing.

Carmakers have argued the targets are unrealistic: the SMMT industry body says battery cars are 26.6 per cent of new sales this year against a 2026 target of 33 per cent, though October reached 32 per cent. Green and some Labour MPs, charging firms and EV businesses warn that moving the goalposts would damage investment and climate credibility.
stories.headline: Government expected to cut 2030 electric car sales target from 80% to about 60%
stories.standfirst: Ministers say no decision has been taken, but a Downing Street meeting on Wednesday is expected to settle the change.

body: A gunman opened fire in Krakow's Main Square on Saturday, killing six people, four Polish citizens, one British citizen and one Austrian, and wounding 15, including two police officers. The British victim has not been named. Police shot and wounded the attacker, a 24-year-old Polish man, and he died in hospital early on Monday.

Officials say he held a firearms licence, probably used a legally owned weapon and had no criminal record. The interior minister said he was fascinated by far-right ideologies. The bodies of his parents and sister were later found with gunshot wounds at his home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 150km away.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it terrorism and Poland began two days of national mourning. Investigators are now working on how he obtained his weapons and whether anyone else knew of his plans.
stories.headline: Briton among six killed in Krakow mass shooting; gunman dies in hospital
stories.standfirst: Poland is treating Saturday's attack in the city's Main Square as terrorism, its deadliest shooting since 1989.

body: Lando Norris led from pole to win a wet-dry-wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday. Max Verstappen, who started from the back after an engine penalty, charged through to second, and his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar was third. George Russell and Kimi Antonelli were fourth and fifth for Mercedes, and Oscar Piastri sixth. Antonelli kept fifth despite a five-second penalty for an unsafe release; Charles Leclerc's penalty for hitting Liam Lawson dropped him to eighth.

The points sealed Mercedes' constructors' title, on 652 points to Ferrari's 510. Antonelli has 390 points to Verstappen's 279, a 111-point lead that the three remaining races cannot overturn. McLaren are fourth in the constructors' table on 398, 17 behind Red Bull, with Norris sixth among drivers.
Ferrari's afternoon unravelled into public recriminations between Lewis Hamilton and the pit wall. Next up is Las Vegas on 22 November.
stories.headline: Norris wins wet Brazilian Grand Prix as Mercedes clinch constructors' title
stories.standfirst: McLaren's Lando Norris converted pole into victory at Interlagos, while Kimi Antonelli's lead in the drivers' standings is now out of reach.

body: Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT in late October. On Monday Reuters reported that the company had emailed bankers a price range of $70 to $80 a share for about 867 million shares, which would raise up to $69.3bn and imply a valuation of around $1.4 trillion. Anthropic then withdrew the email and said the correct pricing would be announced soon.

According to the Wall Street Journal, trading could begin as soon as late next week. Backers had been hoping for about $1.5 trillion only a week ago, and some now want a lower figure. Anthropic's latest filing reported third-quarter revenue of about $17bn, more than ten times a year earlier, alongside a large net loss and close to $900bn of spending commitments stretching to 2045.
stories.headline: Anthropic withdraws reported $70 to $80 IPO price range as listing nears
stories.standfirst: A Reuters report put the share sale at up to $69bn before the company said a corrected price would follow.

body: Security firm Malbear Labs has published details of what it calls Operation Snowball, after finding an openly accessible directory containing about 70 session logs from an AI-driven hacking setup. The operator had wrapped a DeepSeek model in a 78,000-character jailbreak prompt covering 21 categories of offensive work and let it run attacks.

Over more than two weeks the tool targeted a European telecoms provider and 13 organisations hosted on its systems, mainly through CVE-2026-20320, a flaw in Cisco's BroadWorks Xtended Services Platform that lets an attacker read data without logging in. It then installed the open-source Sliver remote-control framework.
The researchers stress the outcomes are not independently verified and the evidence does not establish who was behind it or whether a state was involved.
stories.headline: Exposed server reveals AI agent used to hack a European telecoms provider
stories.standfirst: Researchers found transcripts of an automated hacking tool built on a DeepSeek model that exploited a Cisco flaw.

body: The UN's annual climate conference opened on Monday in Antalya and runs until 20 November. Turkey hosts and holds the presidency through its environment minister, Murat Kurum, while Australia steers the negotiations, a compromise after both countries bid to host. The US has sent no official government delegation after Donald Trump withdrew from the Paris Agreement, though some members of Congress and US businesses are attending.

Turkey is promoting a goal of electricity meeting 35 per cent of energy demand by 2035. A transition away from fossil fuels is not on the negotiated agenda, which campaigners criticise. The sharpest fights are expected over money: how to deliver the pledge to triple finance helping poorer countries adapt, and who pays. A second global stocktake of progress under the Paris deal also begins. Andy Burnham is due to attend this week.
stories.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Turkey with no US delegation
stories.standfirst: Two weeks of talks in Antalya start under an unusual split presidency, with fossil fuels off the formal agenda.

body: President Isaac Herzog on Saturday gave Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar! party and a former military chief of staff, the first chance to form a government after the 27 October election. Parties with 67 MKs recommended Eisenkot in consultations, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu; United Torah Judaism backed neither.

The arithmetic is awkward. Netanyahu's coalition won 53 seats, Eisenkot's bloc 48 and two Arab-led parties, Raam and the Joint List, a record 19; a majority needs 61. Some right-wing parties in Eisenkot's camp say they will not join a government that relies on Arab parties, yet he may need Raam and the Joint List to back a minority government, and both have conditions he has not met. Courting ultra-Orthodox parties instead would mean concessions on military conscription that his own supporters oppose.

His mandate runs to 6 December, extendable to 20 December. If he fails, Herzog is likely to turn to Netanyahu, who stays caretaker prime minister and has warned against a government backed by what he calls supporters of terrorism. Eisenkot's party says it does not rule out a unity government on its own terms. If nobody succeeds, Israel goes back to the polls.
stories.headline: Israel's president asks Gadi Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, to form the next government

sources.name: The New York Times via Boston Globe

stories.standfirst: Parties holding 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats recommended the former army chief after an inconclusive election, but a working majority is not yet in sight.

COP31 continues in Antalya until 20 November; Andy Burnham is due this week.
